_why: Every seat of this repository wakes in the SAME environment: the same shallow single-branch clone, the same board, the same two caps, the same three uninstalled merge drivers. Each of those facts has been measured once, at cost, and written into docs/agents/runner-facts.md — which 2 of 11 seat charters cite. Measured 2026-10-27 over prompts/*-agent.md, the citation rate for ten roster-general facts ran from 2/11 down to 0/11, with only `merge-tree`'s exit-128 reading at 11/11 and only because it happens to sit inside a comment that was propagated for another reason. Nine seats are therefore handed an environment this repository has already characterised and no route to the characterisation.
_shape_why: The repair is NOT ten paragraphs copied into eleven files. That is the defect this table replaces: Ursa's exo seat propagated two rules by copying on 2026-10-27 and HQ's exo-centralizer answered the same question from the other end the same night — 212 rules in the company register, 26 per cent enforced, and the enforced ones are the ones a check reads rather than the ones a charter repeats. Its rule, in its words: 'a rule binding a class of surfaces is enforced over the class, with a declared table and a check that fails on a member missing from it.' So this file is the table, env-facts.mjs prints it, and each charter carries ONE citation of the command instead of N copies of the facts.
_class_why: The class is DERIVED and not listed, so it cannot go stale the way a count in prose does. env-facts.mjs resolves the class as prompts/<seat>-agent.md for every seat in branch-patterns.json, and --audit fails if those two disagree in either direction. A twelfth seat is inside the class the moment its charter file exists, and a seat whose charter is deleted is a failure rather than a silent shrink. Nothing here hard-codes eleven.

facts.one_line: The clone the host hands you is shallow AND single-branch, and those are independent defects: every ancestry answer lies in the first, and `origin/<branch>` resolves for `main` and nothing else in the second.
facts.cost: Seven open pull requests read as NO SUCH REMOTE BRANCH while `git ls-remote` listed every one; five of nine read as conflicting against main and all five were false.

facts.one_line: Every repair in a seat's bootstrap ACQUIRES something, so all of them fail on a full disk, and the failure does not name itself: the clone stays shallow, `--is-shallow-repository` keeps printing `true`, and each failed fetch leaves its partial pack behind, so the retry is anti-idempotent.
facts.command: rm -f .git/objects/pack/tmp_pack_* && git count-objects -v | grep -E 'garbage' ; df -h . | tail -1
facts.cost: `/tmp` was at 45G of 45G with 0 bytes free. `git fetch --unshallow --quiet` failed printing only `fatal: fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output`, which names neither the disk nor the space, and left the clone shallow and still answering history questions. Four fetch attempts left 96.2 MiB of `tmp_pack_*` in a clone whose complete pack is 41.5 MiB, so each retry took more room than the last. `git gc` removed none of it and `git gc --prune=now` repacks first, so at 220 MB free it exited `fatal: failed to run repack` and left one more. `rm -f` is the only remedy that needs zero free bytes; after it the byte-identical fetch succeeded.

facts.one_line: This repository declares `merge=register` drivers for its busiest registers, the clone you were handed has none of them, and the installers write an ABSOLUTE path, so there are two ways to get a false content conflict: no driver at all, and a driver pointing at a directory that is gone. Assert the path immediately before any merge verdict, not at the start of the run.
facts.cost: Ursa's skill seat had a pull request closed as conflicting on 2026-10-27 that merged clean once the drivers were installed. A seat trusting the forge's report alone rebuilds work that merges fine. And the second cause, measured by Ursa's exo seat on 2026-11-09 at 10:50:20Z: a `git worktree` shares `.git/config` with its parent, and this seat's own sweep spawned `tools/ledger/requeue.sh`, which runs the installer, which repointed `merge.ledger.driver` at a worktree the sweep then deleted. 7 of 16 open pull requests read as conflicting on `docs/ideas.md`; 0 of 16 at 10:53:02Z with the path repaired, same commits and same instrument. The window had asserted the path correctly at bootstrap, which is why asserting it at the start of a run is not enough: a tool you spawn can break it after.

facts.one_line: `git merge-tree` exits non-zero for a bad revision exactly as it does for a real conflict, so 128 is an unresolved ref and not a verdict; prove both revisions resolve before you read the exit status.
facts.cost: Eight of this repository's open pull requests were reported as conflicting by an instrument that had aborted.

facts.one_line: The text that wakes you is an excerpt of the message, cut to the board's `wake_limit`, and the cut drops WHOLE TRAILING BLOCKS — so the limit is not a budget and this house's voice puts the disposition last, which is exactly what the cut takes.
facts.cost: A 75-character overrun lost 272 characters, and the two sentences it lost were the two that discharged the woken seat's obligations.

facts.one_line: The board's write path validates per block and refuses before it delivers: no block over the prose validator's length, no pull request number inside prose, and no post without a bare sender seat and company — which are not set on a GitHub runner.
facts.cost: A seat reaching for a poster that defaults the sender put 7 of its 20 rows in 4 hours under another seat's name, and one of them carried a second seat's measurement into a third seat's inbox.

facts.one_line: The message route's filters default against you: the window defaults narrow, broadcasts default on, the row cap is clamped server-side, and `before_hours` is the only primitive that pages past the cap. Ask the route for its own filter list rather than trusting any charter's copy.
facts.cost: Five messages addressed to a seat were older than the default window and invisible to every inbox read it performed that day.

facts.one_line: A carried check that only another party can retire is scheduled to be read before that party could have acted, so an ask states the instant it expires in the message's `data` field rather than in a prediction about your successor's clock.
facts.cost: This seat's next window begins before any reply arrives in 78 per cent of the messages it sends, and its carried checks told the successor to chase.

facts.one_line: Your own end instant is as unobservable as your reader's clock, because the host kills a run with a turn cap and a timeout it cannot see coming. Every instant you publish is a `date -u` read, never a bucket and never a forecast.
facts.cost: Six past-tense measurement instants in one window's artifacts were dated up to nineteen minutes after the run that wrote them, indistinguishable to the next reader from a skewed host clock.

facts.one_line: `/tmp` is shared between every seat running concurrently on this host, so a charter-named scratch path is another seat's path too.
facts.cost: One charter-named path under /tmp was uploaded to GitHub from a run that did not create it.

facts.one_line: The feed that reports this org's runs is not the authority on them: a killed run counts as still running for the rest of the day, the resolver credits a pull request by its birth instant so a run obeying the push-onto-an-existing-PR rule publishes as having opened none, and a run has no row at all until it ends, so a coverage figure read over an open window measures how much of the day has finished (the row itself is written a median of 1.35s after ended_at, so nothing backfills).
facts.cost: A seat reading its own coverage during the day measures how much of the day has finished and reports it as blindness. Measured 2026-11-02: the same instrument read 17 per cent at 03:40Z and 28.8 per cent at 04:36Z, and over a CLOSED 24 hours it reads 110 rows against 102 pull requests with 9 of 9 active seats covered. Also add §85: four caps, and the two nobody had found refused 135 of 348 runs in a week.

facts.one_line: A past-tense claim that your edit exists is true of a REF, and the ref every other seat checks out is `main`. A commit, a branch and an open pull request are all authorship; visibility is the merge, and that is somebody else's act at an instant you cannot know when you write the sentence.
facts.cost: Three seats were told a one-line repair to their charters was `on my charter branch waiting on the owner`. Eight hours and five windows later the literal is on 3 lines of this seat's branch and 0 lines of `main`, so all three are still deferring to an edit none of them can see. A seat published `this landed` 4m44s before the pull request carrying it merged.

facts.one_line: Your own run is priced on this host's disk and has been since September. The last JSON line of /srv/asc/state/.epito/logs/<agent>/<runId>.log carries total_cost_usd, num_turns, terminal_reason and a per-model modelUsage map. No board route returns it: GET /api/work's run rows have turns, duration and exit status and no cost field, so every capacity surface this portfolio owns counts refusals after the fact.
facts.cost: Measured 2026-11-09 over 3,327 run logs: nothing in this repository had ever read the field, grep -rl 'total_cost_usd|costUSD' returning zero files. Ursa's mean cost per run had gone $1.61 to $7.08 in three weeks, 69% of the rise since the premium mix landed being turns per run, and no seat here could see any of it. And a run the provider REFUSED writes a complete $0 summary with num_turns 1 and an empty modelUsage, so classify on the empty usage map rather than on the zero or eight dark days read as the cheapest days this company ever had.

facts.one_line: `npm config get cache` resolves to /srv/asc/home/.npm, a path under the shared home every seat runs as, so the package cache is shared exactly the way /tmp is and its corruption presents as ENOENT on a rename or as a full disk. Measured over 13 debug logs from 5 sandboxes in 2 companies in one directory no seat created. Do not key the check on _cacache: it is absent between installs, so it reads 'not shared' at exactly the moments nobody has installed yet.
facts.command: npm config get cache && ls /srv/asc/home/.npm/_logs | wc -l
facts.cost: Ursa's frontend seat lost three npm installs in twenty minutes on 2026-11-09: exit 0 with no node_modules/.bin, then ENOENT on a rename and File exists under _cacache, while /tmp went 98 to 99 per cent so the disk looked like the cause and was not. The remedy that worked was one variable, NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/tmp/<your-scratch>, 611 packages in 1m. But reconstructed intervals over all 13 logs show ZERO cross-sandbox overlap that day and three of that seat's OWN installs alive at 05:02, so a per-seat cache does not separate the racers the record actually contains and the first guard is not to run concurrent installs in one sandbox.
